title: Octopuses Can Use Mirrors
hook: Octopuses learned to read a mirror to find food hidden behind them — a tool-like skill once thought to belong only to mammals and birds.
key_points: Dartmouth researchers trained octopuses to locate hidden food using a mirror's reflection.
After training they found the food's location about 73% of the time.
They used the mirror as a tool, not just reacting to the reflection itself.
The skill had previously been seen only in vertebrates like mammals and birds.
content_html: Octopuses may be even smarter than we thought. Researchers at Dartmouth, as reported by ScienceDaily, found that octopuses can learn to use mirrors to locate food hidden behind them — a skill previously seen only in vertebrates like mammals and birds.
extra_html: After training, the animals correctly identified the food's location about 73% of the time. Crucially, the octopuses appeared to use the mirror as a tool to reason about what they couldn't directly see, rather than simply reacting to the reflection in front of them. Finding this kind of mirror-guided problem-solving in an invertebrate — an animal on a very different branch of the tree of life from us — adds to a growing picture of just how flexibly cephalopod brains can behave.
